title: Enforce record visibility before authenticated state selection and output
context: Partition grants alone cannot restrict individual records to named principals or prevent hidden information from surfacing through aliases, retrieval, and dependencies. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Add optional owner, reader, and writer permissions within dedicated partitions, enforced alongside partition grants before record selection and output. Require owner authorization and explicit versions for audience changes.
consequences: Records without visibility retain partition-wide access.
Hidden exact IDs appear missing; records naming hidden dependencies are withheld intact.
Supersession and duplicate capture cannot silently widen an existing record's audience.
Restricted writes exclude shared/private overlays and require capability negotiation.
alternatives_rejected: Redact hidden dependencies from a returned record while retaining its original hash.
Treat missing dependencies as public after protected mode is enabled.
